title: ruling needed(components/core): PageHeaderRenderer ranks `titleFormat` ABOVE the declared name pointer — the opposite of `getRecordDisplayName`'s documented ADR-0079 precedence
body:
Filed by the `domain:ui` PM seat (`session_01YBWFb5YgMU5dw8p2VKj16S`) on behalf of the objectui#8175 dev, who found it while making `record:details`' dedupe ladder agree with the header chain and correctly refused to fold it in — **closing it changes what the H1 shows**, which is a product ruling, not a repair. ⛔ Not claimed, ⛔ not graded.

## What

Two implementations of the same ADR-0079 concept order two rungs differently:

- **`@object-ui/core`'s `getRecordDisplayName`** documents `titleFormat` at **step 3**, i.e. **BELOW** the declared pointer (`nameField` / `displayNameField`).
- **`PageHeaderRenderer`** (`packages/components/src/renderers/layout/containers.tsx`) ranks the interpolated `titleFormat` template **ABOVE** the declared pointer. This is not incidental — it is pinned green today, in `packages/components/src/__tests__/page-header-title.test.tsx` as `titleFormat still outranks nameField`.

So on an object that declares both, the two answer differently, and the currently-green pin is the one asserting the divergent order.

## Why it surfaced now

objectui#8175 (PR #8349) taught `record:details`' dedupe ladder to lead with the resolver instead of a six-entry literal walk, so that the grid hides the row the H1 is showing. That works everywhere the two chains agree. On a `titleFormat` object the ladder now hides **the resolver's field** where it used to hide **the literal walk's** — and *neither* is what the H1 displays, because the H1 is showing an interpolated template that names no single field at all.

⚠️ That is not a regression introduced by objectui#8175: the ladder was wrong on these objects before and is wrong differently now. It is the same defect made visible.

## The related second case, recorded so it is not lost

`page:header`'s own `schema.title`: when an author sets it, the H1 is an arbitrary interpolated string and the dedupe still hides a row no heading is showing. `plugin-detail` cannot see the header schema at all, so nothing in that package can answer it.

**Common shape:** both are rungs that **name no field**. A dedupe keyed on "which single field is the H1" is structurally unable to answer them.

## Options — this is the ruling being asked for

- **A — leave both.** Current behaviour is no worse than before objectui#8175, and a dedupe keyed on one field genuinely cannot answer a rung that names none. Cost: on `titleFormat` objects a grid row still vanishes for no visible reason.
- **B — suppress the dedupe when `objectSchema.titleFormat` is present and fully interpolates.** Hide nothing, because the H1 is not any one field's value. Cheap and local to `plugin-detail`; does **not** touch `schema.title`, which stays invisible to that package.
- **C — close the ordering divergence at its source in `@object-ui/components`,** so the header stops ranking the legacy template above the ADR-0079 pointer. This is the contract-first answer and the only one that makes the two implementations one. ⚠️ It **changes what the H1 shows** on existing records and **contradicts a currently-green pin**, so it is squarely a maintainer ruling.

**Reporting dev's recommendation, and the PM's:** **A** now (nothing is blocked, and PR #8349 is a strict improvement without it), with **B** as its own card if record pages carrying a `titleFormat` turn out to be common. **C** is the real ADR-0079 question and needs the maintainer, because it moves user-visible output and retires a green pin.

## Related

objectui#8175 / PR #8349 (where it was measured) · objectui#7287 / PR #7585 · objectui#7586 · objectui#6843 · objectui#7021 · ADR-0079

## Dedup

`search_issues` over open issues for `titleFormat` / `nameField` / `getRecordDisplayName` / `ADR-0079` — 7 hits, all read. Nearest: objectui#6843 (the record-key probe's stale "step 3b" name) and objectui#7021 (the record-title key in three spellings) — both about the same machinery, neither about the precedence between these two rungs. objectui#8175 is the card this was split out of.
